component: IMAP trash-folder preference and server encoding boundary

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: Fresh full one-file42-line public patch read. DiscoveryDone compares a stored UTF-8 trash-folder preference with a server path. When UTF8=ACCEPT is enabled the server path is copied; otherwise MUTF-7 is converted through UTF-16 to UTF-8 before comparison and clearing a mismatched Trash flag. Fixed selected source retains that exact direction. Selected SetTrashFolderName is the opposite boundary: UTF-8 preference text is converted to MUTF-7 only for non-UTF8 folder lookup, then the original UTF-8 chvalue is stored. The settings picker likewise converts its JS Unicode path only for a traditional-MUTF7 URI. Do not paraphrase these different consumers as one global conversion direction; the uplift prose describes the setter-style direction, while this assigned DiscoveryDone hunk converts server to preference encoding. Exact unavailable discussion keeps this public source-only knowledge at zero full-audit credit. No runtime or test ran.
title: Compare server trash paths in the preference encoding at discovery
